title: Philly Cheesesteak Skillet
subtitle: Melted provolone, peppers, one pan
description: Melted provolone, peppers, one pan. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

steps.title: Slice beef paper-thin
steps.instruction: Partially freeze ribeye 20 minutes; slice as thin as possible against the grain.

steps.title: Sear beef and peppers
steps.instruction: Hot cast iron: sear beef in batches with onions and peppers until edges char. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Melt provolone
steps.instruction: Pile beef mixture; lay provolone over top. Cover 1 minute until cheese melts into the meat.

steps.title: Fill hoagies
steps.instruction: Scoop into toasted hoagie rolls. Philly Cheesesteak Skillet should drip a little — that's the point.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Philly Cheesesteak Skillet with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Philly Cheesesteak Skillet on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Melted provolone, peppers, one pan. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.

adaptable.note: Use a certified gluten-free bun/bread and toast on a separate, clean surface.
